title: Phase 3: Secret Management - Provider System
description: Design and implement pluggable secret provider system with env: and file: providers for MVP, including credential_ref parsing and secret caching.
design:
- Define SecretProvider interface
- Implement credential_ref parser (protocol:path)
- Implement provider registry
- Implement env: provider (os.Getenv)
- Implement file: provider with permission checks (0600)
- Implement secret caching with TTL (5 minutes)
- Define error types for secret operations
acceptance_criteria:
- SecretProvider interface defined and documented
- env:VAR_NAME retrieves from environment
- file:/path/to/secret reads file content
- file: provider enforces 0600 permissions
- Secret cache works with TTL
- Unit tests for all providers pass
- Integration test fetches secrets successfully

title: Phase 4: Authentication - Strategy System
description: Design and implement pluggable authentication strategy system with bearer token and header template strategies for MVP.
design:
- Define AuthStrategy interface
- Implement strategy registry
- Implement bearer token strategy (Authorization header)
- Implement header template strategy (custom headers)
- Request cloning mechanism to avoid mutations
- Strategy selection based on service config
acceptance_criteria:
- AuthStrategy interface defined and documented
- Bearer strategy injects Authorization header correctly
- Header strategy injects custom headers
- Original request is not modified
- Unit tests for all strategies pass
- Integration test verifies header injection

title: Phase 2: MITM Core - Selective TLS Termination
description: Implement selective TLS MITM for configured domains, including CA certificate generation, dynamic leaf certificate creation, and domain-based routing decisions.
design:
- CA certificate generation and secure storage
- Dynamic leaf certificate generation (signed by CA)
- Certificate caching mechanism (sync.Map)
- Domain matching logic (exact match for MVP)
- TLS handshake handling (client and upstream)
- HTTP request/response proxying through TLS
- Certificate trust validation and documentation
acceptance_criteria:
- CA certificate generated on first run
- CA stored securely in ~/.config/chaperone/
- Leaf certificates generated per-domain
- TLS handshake succeeds with client
- HTTP requests decrypted and proxied
- Integration test with api.openai.com succeeds
- User can manually trust CA certificate

design:
NOTE: Basic test infrastructure (testify, helpers, fixtures) is established in Phase 0.5. This phase focuses on complete system validation.

- Write E2E test with real OpenAI API call (requires API key)

- Run go vet and fix all issues

title: Phase 5: Service Engine - Configuration and Policy
description: Implement service configuration structures, service registry, and policy enforcement for path/method allowlists and request size limits.
design:
- Define Service and Policy configuration structures
- Implement service registry (map keyed by host_pattern)
- Implement service lookup by hostname (exact match)
- Implement path allowlist checking (glob matching)
- Implement method allowlist checking
- Implement request body size limit enforcement
- Integrate with MITM handler, secret providers, and auth strategies
acceptance_criteria:
- Service config structure defined
- Service registry loads services
- Service lookup returns correct service by hostname
- Path allowlist blocks disallowed paths (403)
- Method allowlist blocks disallowed methods (403)
- Body size limit enforced
- Integration test verifies policy enforcement
